title: Tumor-related aphasia: Risk assessment with TMS mapping and long-term assessment of aphasia in patients with intracranial tumors
summary:
Background:
Brain tumors can affect a person’s ability to speak, both before and after surgery. To protect language as well as possible, we can map language areas in the brain prior to surgery, using a method called transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). This technique stimulates the brain to identify regions that are important for language. Usually, this is done with a single task (object naming). However, language consists of many different abilities, so one task alone may not be sufficient. In addition, little is known about how language problems develop over a longer period of time after tumor surgery.

Aim of the study:
The study addresses two main questions. First, it examines whether a new TMS language task (sentence completion) is better at identifying important language areas in the brain than the commonly used object naming task. Second, it investigates how language abilities change over time after tumor surgery and which factors may influence this recovery.

Methods:
The study includes patients who are scheduled to undergo surgery to remove a brain tumor. Before surgery, a language mapping is conducted using TMS. Here, patients perform two different language tasks, which are then compared. After surgery, language skills are tested at several time points to track changes over time. The study does not interfere with medical treatment but accompanies routine clinical examinations. All collected data are treated confidentially.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of eye, brain and other parts of central nervous system

interventions.name: Study arm 1 focuses on preoperative language mapping using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). The mapping is conducted using not only the standard task of object naming but also a newly developed task assessing word retrieval in a situational sentence context (sentence completion). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspected brain tumor (imaging-based suspected diagnosis), clinically assessed relevant risk of postoperative speech disorder
Exclusion criteria:
Preoperative language level below the requirements of the language tasks performed, contraindications for transcranial magnetic stimulation (cardiac pacemaker, cochlear implant,  intracranial clips)
